grammar_rules.summary: The verb devoir can express a debt, both literal and figurative.
grammar_rules.explanation: Devoir is used to indicate owing something to someone, such as money or a life.
usage: To express owing money or something owed

attestations.section_title: The verb devoir (to have to, must)
attestations.source_text: Devoir as a debt

grammar_rules.explanation: Devoir is used to say that someone must do something.
grammar_rules.negative_form: Vous ne devez pas y aller.
grammar_rules.affirmative_form: Vous devez assister à la réunion demain matin.

attestations.section_title: The verb devoir (to have to, must)
attestations.source_text: Devoir as an obligation

grammar_rules.summary: Devoir can express probability or supposition.
grammar_rules.explanation: Devoir is used to indicate that something is supposed to happen or is likely.
grammar_rules.affirmative_form: L'avion doit atterrir à dix heures.

attestations.section_title: The verb devoir (to have to, must)
attestations.source_text: Devoir as a probability

grammar_rules.summary: In the conditional or past conditional, devoir means should or should have.
grammar_rules.explanation: When used in the conditional, devoir takes on the meaning of should; in the past conditional, should have.
usage: To give advice, warning, or suggestion
conditions: Used in conditional or past conditional
grammar_rules.negative_form: Tu ne devrais pas lui prêter d'argent.
grammar_rules.affirmative_form: Elles devraient apprendre une langue étrangère.

grammar_rules.summary: Il y a is an impersonal expression meaning there is/there are, and is used in fixed expressions.
grammar_rules.explanation: Il y a introduces existence and is also part of idiomatic expressions.
grammar_rules.formation: il y a + noun / il n'y a plus + noun / il n'y a qu'à + infinitive / il y avait une fois
grammar_rules.negative_form: Il n'y a plus rien dans le frigo.
grammar_rules.affirmative_form: Il y a un chat sur le canapé.

grammar_rules.summary: Il s'agit de is a fixed expression introducing the subject of a work or situation.
grammar_rules.explanation: Il s'agit de is used to state what something is about or what is at stake.
grammar_rules.formation: il s'agit de + noun / il s'agit de + infinitive / il ne s'agit pas de + noun/infinitive
usage: To express necessity (il s'agit de faire vite)
grammar_rules.negative_form: Il ne s'agit pas de plaisanter.
grammar_rules.affirmative_form: Dans ce film, il s'agit d'un crime.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Conjugation of verbs ending in -eindre and -aindre
grammar_rules.summary: Verbs ending in -eindre or -aindre follow a similar conjugation pattern in the present tense.
grammar_rules.explanation: These -re verbs have a stem ending in -ein-/-ain- in the singular, and -eign-/-aign- in the plural forms.
grammar_rules.formation: Singular: stem + s, s, t; Plural: stem + ons, ez, ent (with -eign- or -aign-)
usage: To conjugate peindre, craindre, and similar verbs

attestations.section_title: Verbs ending in -eindre and -aindre
attestations.source_text: Among the -re verbs, some verbs ending in -eindre or -aindre can be grouped together. Verbs like peindre (to paint) include teindre (to dye), ceindre (to encircle), feindre (to feign), craindre (to fear), plaindre (to pity), and se plaindre (to complain).

exceptions_and_traps.title: Devoir: obligation vs probability ambiguity
exceptions_and_traps.description: The meaning of devoir (obligation vs probability) is often determined by voice intonation and gestures.

attestations.section_title: The verb devoir (to have to, must)
attestations.source_text: The voice intonation will often determine if devoir implies an obligation or a probability. For example, il doit venir ce soir, may mean he is supposed to come tonight or he must come tonight. Pay attention to intonation and gestures.
